findings.title: Sensitive card data (PAN, CVV/CVC/CAV2/CID, track/magstripe) appears to be passed to a logger. PCI DSS 3.2 prohibits storing CVV at all, and PAN must be masked (display first-6 + last-4 only). Mask or drop the value before logging.
findings.description: Sensitive card data (PAN, CVV/CVC/CAV2/CID, track/magstripe) appears to be passed to a logger. PCI DSS 3.2 prohibits storing CVV at all, and PAN must be masked (display first-6 + last-4 only). Mask or drop the value before logging.

exploit.payload: Login as alice, POST /api/payments/charge with marker PAN=4111111111111111 and CVV=123, then GET /api/payments/logs and confirm PAN/CVV appear in the log buffer
exploit.expected_signal: Log line containing pan=4111111111111111 and cvv=123 returned from /api/payments/logs
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: Card PAN/CVV visible in log entry: charge user=alice pan=4111111111111111 cvv=123 amount=-9999.99
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: Card PAN/CVV visible in log entry: charge user=alice pan=4111111111111111 cvv=123 amount=-9999.99

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: Removes CVV from the log statement entirely (PCI DSS 3.2 forbids storing CVV in any form, including logs) and masks the PAN to show only the first 6 and last 4 digits, padding the middle with asterisks. The fix is inlined so no new helper symbol is introduced, and it preserves the existing structured-logging idiom used elsewhere in the file.

findings.title: Payment-gateway callback handler trusts amount from the request without re-fetching the authoritative amount from your DB. Webhook callers can be spoofed (or replayed with altered values) -- always reconcile against your own order record before marking the order settled.
findings.description: Payment-gateway callback handler trusts amount from the request without re-fetching the authoritative amount from your DB. Webhook callers can be spoofed (or replayed with altered values) -- always reconcile against your own order record before marking the order settled.

exploit.payload: POST /api/webhook/gateway with orderId=order-1001 and amount=0.01 to settle a $75.00 order at a tampered amount without server-side reconciliation
exploit.expected_signal: Order order-1001 returns status=settled with amount=0.01 (originally 75.00)
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: order order-1001 settled at tampered amount=0.01 (original=75.0); webhook accepted without reconciliation
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: order order-1001 settled at tampered amount=0.01 (original=75.0); webhook accepted without reconciliation

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: Instead of overwriting the order's amount with the value supplied in the webhook payload, we reconcile the incoming amount against the authoritative server-side order record. If the webhook's amount does not match the stored order amount, the request is rejected with 400 and the order is left untouched, preventing spoofed/replayed callers from settling an order at a tampered amount.
references: OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures

notes: validator: logical-equivalence review PASSED — behavior preserved for legitimate inputs. Patch replaces blind overwrite of order.Amount with a verification check that rejects the webhook when the callback amount doesn't match the stored order amount before marking it settled.
validator: tests pass AND exploit no longer reproduces

findings.title: Account/order/payment record is fetched by a caller-supplied id with no ownership check. Classic IDOR -- User A can read User B's account by changing the URL parameter. Verify the authenticated user owns the resource before returning it (e.g. UserId == User.GetUserId()).
findings.description: Account/order/payment record is fetched by a caller-supplied id with no ownership check. Classic IDOR -- User A can read User B's account by changing the URL parameter. Verify the authenticated user owns the resource before returning it (e.g. UserId == User.GetUserId()).

exploit.payload: Authenticate as alice (alice/alice-pw), then GET /api/account/bob using alice's Bearer token — no ownership check exists so bob's balance is returned
exploit.expected_signal: HTTP 200 with bob's account JSON {id:'bob', balance:500} returned to alice's token
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: alice's token read bob's account - id=bob balance=500
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: alice's token read bob's account - id=bob balance=500

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: Resolves the authenticated principal from the bearer token via db.Tokens and rejects the request with 403 Forbid when the caller is not the owner of the requested account id. This closes the IDOR by enforcing that UserId == authenticated user before returning any account data, while preserving the original NotFound/Ok response shape.

findings.title: Payment-mutating endpoint persists a transaction/charge without checking for an Idempotency-Key header against a dedup store. Network retries and double-clicks will create duplicate charges. Require Idempotency-Key, persist (key -> response) with a TTL, and return the cached response on replay.
findings.description: Payment-mutating endpoint persists a transaction/charge without checking for an Idempotency-Key header against a dedup store. Network retries and double-clicks will create duplicate charges. Require Idempotency-Key, persist (key -> response) with a TTL, and return the cached response on replay.

exploit.payload: Authenticate as seeded user alice, then POST /api/payments/transfer twice with identical body and no Idempotency-Key header
exploit.expected_signal: Two successful responses with different transaction_id values proving duplicate transfers were persisted
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: duplicate transfers created without Idempotency-Key tx1=525ab57d623548ed tx2=a53e23178e18431d
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: duplicate transfers created without Idempotency-Key tx1=525ab57d623548ed tx2=a53e23178e18431d

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: The transfer endpoint now requires an Idempotency-Key header and persists (key -> {user, request hash, txId, amount, createdAt}) in a thread-safe ConcurrentDictionary on PaymentsStore. On replay with the same key, the original transaction_id is returned and no new TxRecord is appended; mismatched user/body for the same key returns 409 Conflict. A 24-hour TTL sweep removes stale entries, and TryAdd guards against a race where two concurrent requests share a key.
